summary: John's 8th-great-grandfather; Philipstown (Hudson Highlands) pioneer, called 'Captain', commissioner of highways for Dutchess County.
bio:
Thomas Davenport was born in 1682 (Davenport family Bible) and died in 1759; his will was dated 1746 and proved 1760. He was a pioneer of Philipstown in the Hudson Highlands, commissioner of highways for Dutchess County 1745-49, and called 'Captain'. In 1752 he deeded Goshen-precinct land to his daughter 'Charity Lamoree, wife of John Lamoree'. Westchester deeds show William Davenport senior of the Manor of Fordham 'conveyed to my son Thomas Davenport' land, and a 1718 deed names William Jr. and Thomas as 'sons of William Davenport' (probable father). His second wife Elizabeth was 'believed' to be a Leggett sister (WikiTree's chain Leggett -> Richardson -> Mead of Watford rests on that belief; speculative). Family descent from Rev. John Davenport of New Haven is disproven ('the last, we know, to be untrue', Giles & Franklin p.xix), and the Davenport of Bromhall/Bramhall, Cheshire link is unsupported. Possible Society of Colonial Wars qualifying ancestor.

The full text of his will, dated 10 Oct 1746 while he was 'sick and weak in body', is printed in the Davenport genealogy ([R4-S1]). He recovered and lived until at least 25 Aug 1759, when, according to the family Bible, he presented that Bible to his grandson Thomas (born 11 Apr 1750). The will divides his family in two. The first family is sons Thomas and William, plus the children of his married daughters Sarah Mandeville, Mary Henion and Elizabeth Nelson. The second family is seven minor children, Oliver, Charity, Phebe, Robert, Hannah, Stephen and Abigail, left in the care of his wife Elizabeth. He owned at least one enslaved person, left to his wife for bringing up the children ([R4-S1]). The book gives his rank of captain only from the highway-commissioner record of 1745-49, so 'Captain' may be a courtesy or militia title. No militia commission was found, which matters for any Society of Colonial Wars claim. The genealogy gives his death date as 30 Dec 1759 ([R4-S1]).

researchLog.note: Imported from the project handoff (research rounds 1–3, Oct 2026).
Resolved: Which wife was Charity's mother. → The second wife, Elizabeth. The 1746 will groups Charity with the seven minor children she was bringing up.

Round 4 searched without result: Muster Rolls of New York Provincial Troops 1755-1764 (NYHS Collections 1891, archive.org musterrollsofnew24newy full text): no Davenport entries; these rolls start after his commissioner years anyway
Round 4: read the transcript of his 10 Oct 1746 will (two families; seven minors with wife Elizabeth; an enslaved person) and the 1745-49 highway-commissioner record behind 'Captain'.

events.title: Will
events.description: 'Sick and weak in body.' Leaves £30 to wife Elizabeth; £5 to son Thomas (already provided for); £60 to son William; £10 each to the children of daughters Sarah Mandeville, Mary (by Jacobus Henion) and Elizabeth Nelson; residue to minor children Oliver, Charity, Phebe, Robert, Hannah, Stephen and Abigail, boys taking double shares; a Negro is among the goods left to his wife for bringing up the children. Executors: wife Elizabeth, son Thomas and John Nellson. Witnesses: Joseph Geecocks (Jaycox) and Hannah Sobee (Seeley?). [R4-S1]

events.title: Highway commissioner
events.description: Named a commissioner to lay out highways in 1745 and served through 1749, 'designated in the record as Captain Thomas Davenport'; first among Dutchess freeholders in 1740. [R4-S1]
